Method of Attack: Xwo: Python-based bot scanner for reconnaissance; probes IP ranges from C2 servers for default passwords on services (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Memcached, FTP), checks Apache Tomcat for default logins and misconfigurations, searches for SVN, Git, backup paths, rsync utility, and RealVNC data; enables malicious activity but is not malicious itself

Xbash: Malware with ransomware and cryptojacking capabilities targeting Linux and Microsoft servers; looks for unprotected databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB) and deletes them, leaving ransom notes that cannot restore data
MongoLock: Targets unprotected MongoDB databases, wipes them from the server, and demands ransom to restore
Attack Vector: Scanning for unprotected web services reachable over the internet
Using default credentials to access databases and services
Command and control (C2) servers providing IP ranges to scan
Indicators of Compromise: C2 servers associated with MongoLock: s.propub3r6espa33w[.]tk, s.blockchainbdgpzk[.]tk, s.pcrisk[.]xyz, s.rapid7[.]xyz
Domains mimicking security and news organizations (Rapid7, PCRisk, ProPublica)
Use of Cloudflare CDN services for C2 domains
Detection by 37 antivirus engines on VirusTotal
